subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the denary (decimal) value of the binary number 00101101?
When digitising sound, what does the sample rate refer to?
options: The length of the sound file
The number of samples taken per second
The number of bits used to store each sample
The loudness of the recording
questions.explain: Sample rate is the number of samples (measurements of the sound wave) taken each second, measured in hertz.

questions.q: Which character set uses more bits per character and can therefore represent characters from many of the world's languages?
options: ASCII
Denary
Binary
Unicode
questions.explain: Unicode uses more bits per character than ASCII, allowing it to represent a very large range of international characters and symbols.

questions.q: When adding the 8-bit binary numbers 11111111 and 00000001, what occurs?
options: The result is negative
The result fits exactly in 8 bits with no issue
An overflow occurs because the result needs a 9th bit
The numbers cannot be added in binary
questions.explain: 11111111 + 00000001 = 100000000, which needs 9 bits, so an overflow error occurs in an 8-bit register.

questions.q: Which of these is most likely to use lossless compression?
options: A streamed low-quality music preview
A ZIP archive of a text document that must be exactly restored
A heavily compressed JPEG photo for a website
A low-bitrate video clip
questions.explain: Text in a ZIP file must be restored perfectly, so lossless compression is used.

questions.q: What is the key difference between lossy and lossless compression?
options: Lossy permanently removes some data; lossless allows the original to be fully restored
Both remove data permanently and cannot be reversed
Lossless removes data permanently; lossy can be fully reversed
Neither reduces the file size
questions.explain: Lossy compression permanently discards some data to shrink the file, while lossless lets the original be reconstructed exactly.

questions.q: Why is hexadecimal often used by programmers instead of long binary numbers?
options: It uses only the digits 0 and 1
It is shorter and easier for humans to read and less error-prone than binary
Hexadecimal can represent numbers that binary cannot
Computers store data directly in hexadecimal
questions.explain: Hex is a more compact, human-friendly way to write binary, as each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits.

questions.q: In a bitmap image, what does increasing the colour depth (bits per pixel) allow?
options: A greater number of possible colours per pixel
A smaller overall file size
A larger number of pixels in the image
A faster sample rate
questions.explain: Colour depth is the number of bits used per pixel, so more bits means more possible colours.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal value of the binary number 11101010?
options: DA
FA
EA
AE
questions.explain: 1110 = E and 1010 = A, so the value is EA.

questions.q: What is the effect of increasing the bit depth when sampling sound?
options: It increases the accuracy of each sample and the audio quality
It converts the sound to an image
It reduces the number of samples per second
It reduces the file size
questions.explain: A higher bit depth allows each sample to be recorded more precisely, improving sound quality but increasing file size.

questions.q: How many bits does a single hexadecimal digit represent?
questions.explain: One hexadecimal digit represents exactly 4 bits (a nibble).

questions.q: What is the result of a logical right shift of two places applied to the 8-bit number 00011000?
questions.explain: Shifting 00011000 right by two places gives 00000110 (24 becomes 6, a division by 4).
